field.label: Enabled
field.help: Run a synapse-sensor process for this interface. The plugin-wide switch must also be on.

field.label: Name
field.help: Letters, digits and underscores, unique on this firewall. It names the service profile (service synapseids_sensor restart <name>), the rendered configuration /usr/local/etc/synapseids/instances/<name>.conf, the pidfile and the log directory /var/log/synapseids/<name>/, and it is the column the selftest prints beside every check. Naming it after the interface (wan, dmz, iot, mgmt) is the least surprising choice.

field.label: Interface
field.help: The single interface this sensor captures from. One process captures one device: to monitor four segments, create four instances. Two instances may not share an interface.

field.label: Sensor ID
field.help: Identifier this instance reports to the daemon (--sensor-id), shown in the SynapseIDS capture-sources view. It must differ from every other instance's: a packet routed between two monitored segments is legitimately seen twice, and the sensor ID is the only thing that tells the two observations apart.

field.label: Location
field.help: Free-form location label reported to the daemon (--location), e.g. "hq-rack-2".

field.label: Listen address
field.help: Listen mode only: host:port this instance binds (--listen). Every instance is a separate process, so each needs its own port - 0.0.0.0:4789, 0.0.0.0:4790 and so on. Restrict these to the management interface address and add a firewall rule; do not expose them to the internet. Ignored in connect mode.

field.label: Capture filter
field.help: Built-in filter preset (--filter). Leave on "All traffic" to capture every frame this interface sees.

field.label: Direction
field.help: Which direction of traffic to hand to the BPF device (--direction).

field.label: Send
field.help: How much of the analysis runs here on the firewall for this interface, and therefore how much crosses the link (--mode). "Raw packets" streams every frame. "Flow records" aggregates flows here and sends one record per flow — around 1.5% of the raw bandwidth on ordinary traffic. "Feature vectors only" also computes the 48 features here and sends nothing else, so no packet content from this segment ever leaves the firewall — around 1.9% of the raw bandwidth. The classifications are identical in all three modes. Set per instance, so a sensitive internal segment can be feature-only while the WAN stays raw. The two record modes need a SynapseIDS daemon that speaks SYNPOIP v2; an older one refuses the connection rather than silently falling back to sending packets.

field.label: Promiscuous mode
field.help: Also capture frames not addressed to this firewall (--promisc). Required when the interface is fed from a SPAN/mirror port.

field.label: Snap length
field.help: Bytes captured per frame (--snaplen). 262144 keeps whole frames; lower it only to save bandwidth.

field.label: BPF buffer
field.help: BPF store-buffer bytes (--bpf-buffer). Blank uses the 512 KiB default. The kernel clamps this to net.bpf.maxbufsize (also 512 KiB by default), so raising it here only helps once you raise that sysctl too — the sensor log shows requested vs granted at start. A bigger buffer absorbs bursts before the kernel drops frames on a busy WAN edge.

field.label: Description
field.help: Free text, shown in the grid.

field.label: I am authorised to monitor this interface
field.help: Required before this instance can be enabled, and asked separately for every instance. synapse-sensor refuses live capture without --authorized (PROJECT.md 28.18), and being authorised to monitor one segment is not being authorised to monitor another - so this is never copied from another instance and is never set by the grid's enable toggle. Only monitor networks you own or have written permission to monitor.
